The model data of this frame are reproduced from the data set under that licence, converted to this project's input format (changes: 4 elements per member merged into one member, plane model embedded in 3D, 0.8 E entered as the modulus).

analysis: Frame 1 of the data set (single-storey portal frame, fixed bases), units kip and inch. Plane frame in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held (the data set's frames are 'fully braced out-of-plane'); in-plane bending about local z, so the data set's Izz is the section's Iz. Modulus 0.8 E = 23200 ksi (the data set's condition for all elastic analyses; its element table points to E = 29000 ksi, the published results correspond to 0.8 E - verified for this frame with the first-order displacements). No shear deformation. A straight line of the data set's elements is one member here, the loads at its interior nodes are point loads on the member. The data set's model is plane (no out-of-plane buckling of a member between joints); the engine's member is spatial, so Iy = 1000 Izz is entered for every section instead of the listed Iyy: no out-of-plane mode can precede the in-plane behaviour compared, and Iy does not enter the in-plane results. Case 'Right' of the data set: imperfect geometry with every node at x + y/500, lateral loads acting toward +x. First-order (linear) analysis: the data set's 'LA'.

quarantine.diagnosis: One of three targets missed by 1.24 times the tolerance: member 2 (right column) engine 2131.4762 kip in, displayed 2131.47 (stored 2131.47251). Cause: precision of the input listing, not of the analysis. The data set's model file lists loads (and coordinates) with five significant figures, while its results were computed with the unrounded model and are displayed to 0.01 kip in, i.e. to 1e-6 ... 1e-5 of the moments; a load rounded in the fifth figure changes a moment by up to 5e-5 of its value. Evidence: the first-order joint displacements of the same model, displayed with three decimals, are reproduced; every first-order result of this frame (displacements and moments, both cases) exceeds the stored value by the same factor 1 + 1.73e-6, as a load factor would: the loads listed as 34.849 and 348.49 kip are not exactly the loads of the analysis.

limitsNote: The member numbering of the data set is not defined in its files; the identification of the members was inferred from the first-order values (README.md), so these targets are not independent evidence of the identification.
